smoke.cmd: tsx --test test/*.test.ts (tsx binary borrowed from sibling repo quilt-playtest/node_modules/.bin/tsx — this repo ships no node_modules/dist)
smoke.notes: node:test runner via tsx; covers direct-hit tier, confirm tier, compile tier (mock compiler), veto paths, confidence climb, PincherSheet composition, and the three platform sheets incl. .nail loading on ESP32 defaults. Fully offline; the AI compiler cell is exercised only through a mock Compiler.

essence: Reflex engine built entirely from quilt cells: pinch, match, veto, execute — three latency tiers, LLM only as compiler

ideas.name: the whole reflex engine is a sheet of cells
ideas.statement: Every layer of the reflex arc is declared as a cell — pinch (formula), match (program), execute (program), veto (listener), compile (ai), store (vector_store) — so federation, subscription, audit and persistence are inherited from the cell runtime instead of rebuilt per engine.

ideas.name: three-tier escalation on match score
ideas.statement: One pinch, three clocks: score >= 0.80 executes directly (<50ms, no LLM), 0.55-0.80 executes through the confirm tier, below 0.55 with no match the SLOW tier compiles a new reflex via the LLM and stores it — the reflex database grows only at the moments the fast world fails.

ideas.name: the veto is a cell-level gate, not an afterthought
ideas.statement: Before any execution — hit, confirm, or freshly compiled — the veto listener checks the pinch's safety hints (sandbox/network/filesystem) against the reflex's declared constraints; escalation of privilege is refused with a reason, and the refusal is a first-class result kind.

ideas.name: confidence is earned economics for reflexes
ideas.statement: A reflex starts at confidence 0.5 and climbs logarithmically toward 0.99 with hits (0.5 + 0.49*log10(1+hits)); usage history (hits, lastHitAt) plus embedding make reflexes tensors with weight/gravity/distance — hot reflexes live near the agent, cold ones far.

ideas.name: portable agent state: the .nail bundle
ideas.statement: The engine serializes to a content-addressed .nail (reflexes, veto rules, compile history, provenance) that an ESP32-class offline engine loads directly — the same sheet runs on cloud, workstation, and no_std edge, with LLM-dependent cells no-oping without keys.

parts.name: the pinch envelope
parts.essence: Input atom: {trigger, context?, safety?} — a raw trigger string plus optional context and safety hints (sandbox/network/filesystem/timeoutMs) that the veto will check against the reflex's own constraints.

parts.name: the reflex record
parts.essence: Learned pattern: {id, embedding, intent, action, safety, confidence, hits, createdAt, lastHitAt, provenance?} — the unit stored, scored, and executed; provenance records who compiled it and (optionally) its parent reflex.
outputs: Reflex stored in the reflex store

parts.name: brute-force cosine reflex store with upstream federation
parts.essence: MemoryReflexStore scores every entry by cosine similarity and returns top-k; up to ~10K reflexes this beats an HNSW index because the search fits in L2; an optional upstream store mirrors every insert/delete (the federation hook).
parts.gate: cosine returns 0 on dimension mismatch (never throws mid-match)
parts.failure_mode: dimension-mismatched embeddings silently score 0 (safe but invisible without an audit cell)

parts.name: trigger embedding (pluggable embedder)
parts.essence: run() step 1: embed(pinch.trigger); three implementations — CloudflareAIEmbedder (remote), QuiltAIEmbedder, OfflineEmbedder — plus HashEmbedder, a deterministic character-histogram embedder for tests/demos/offline use.
parts.failure_mode: hash embedder is semantic-free: two different triggers can collide; fine for tests, not for production matching

parts.name: top-5 match query
parts.essence: run() step 2: store.query(embedding, 5) — the reflex database is consulted before anything else; empty results fall through to the compile tier.

parts.name: three-way tier router
parts.essence: Routing law: matches[0].score < confirmThreshold -> compile tier; >= hitThreshold -> direct execute (FAST); else confirm-and-execute (MEDIUM). The tier is returned in the result kind so latency budgets are observable per pinch.
parts.gate: score >= 0.80 for direct hit; 0.55 <= score < 0.80 for confirm
parts.failure_mode: an embedding drift that drops all scores below 0.55 silently converts every pinch into an LLM compile (cost spike) — threshold tuning is operational policy

parts.name: reflex execution with timeout
parts.essence: The reflex's action string is evaluated as an async JS expression via new Function with the pinch in scope, raced against a 5s executionTimeoutMs; failures become 'Execution failed: ...' errors.
parts.gate: Promise.race against executionTimeoutMs (default 5000) — a hung reflex cannot hang the engine
parts.failure_mode: HONEST RISK (comment in code): 'In production this would be sandboxed' — today the action runs unsandboxed via eval-in-Function; the veto checks declared hints, not real effects

parts.name: confidence climb (logarithmic hit economics)
parts.essence: Every executed reflex bumps hits and lastHitAt and recomputes confidence = min(0.99, 0.5 + 0.49*log10(1+hits)) — trust in a reflex grows with reuse and saturates below certainty.
parts.gate: confidence clamped to [0.5 start, 0.99 ceiling] — invariant band
parts.failure_mode: confidence measures FREQUENCY not CORRECTNESS: a confidently wrong reflex that keeps matching climbs the same curve

parts.name: compile-and-store (the LLM as compiler)
parts.essence: SLOW tier: compiler.compile(pinch) returns {intent, action}; the new reflex is created at confidence 0.5 with provenance compiledBy:'compiler', veto-checked, inserted, then executed once for the caller — future identical pinches hit the FAST tier.
parts.gate: veto check runs on the FRESH reflex before insert+execute (a compiled reflex can be born vetoed)
parts.failure_mode: without a compiler configured the tier returns an error result rather than hallucinating an action (fail-closed)

parts.name: veto gate (safety before execution)
parts.essence: DefaultVeto compares the pinch's SafetyHints to the reflex's declared constraints and refuses escalation: pinch wants network 'any' but reflex is restricted -> refused; pinch wants filesystem 'any' but reflex restricted -> refused; pinch wants sandbox 'none' but reflex requires wasm -> refused. Every tier (hit/confirm/compiled) passes through it.
parts.gate: no execution without veto.ok — refusal reason becomes the result's 'vetoed' kind
parts.failure_mode: the default veto compares DECLARED hints only; an action that lies about its needs is not caught at this layer

parts.name: tier thresholds as configuration
parts.essence: hitThreshold (0.80) and confirmThreshold (0.55) are constructor policy — the same engine can be tuned more paranoid (raise both) or more reflexive (lower them) without code changes.
parts.gate: thresholds are read once at construction — mid-flight policy changes are not possible (deterministic per engine instance)

parts.name: no-compiler fail-closed path
parts.essence: If the match fails and no Compiler is configured (the ESP32/offline case), run() returns {kind:'error', error:'No match and no compiler configured'} — the engine never invents an action it cannot source.
parts.failure_mode: on the edge this surfaces as an error result rather than a silent fallback — visible in the result stream

parts.name: PincherSheet descriptor (engine as cells)
parts.essence: PincherSheet(config) builds the engine AND declares the six cells {pinch:formula, match:program, execute:program, veto:listener, compile:ai, store:vector_store} with descriptions — the sheet is the public architecture diagram, loadable into any QuiltEngine.
parts.failure_mode: HONEST GAP: the descriptor declares the cells but runPinch still drives sheet.engine.run directly — the cell graph is the architecture contract, not yet the execution path

parts.name: .nail bundle export + ESP32 loadNail
parts.essence: exportNail(name, tier) packages agent state {version, reflexes, vetoRules, compileHistory, metadata}; buildNail produces the EmbeddedNail and ESP32Engine.loadNail boots an offline engine from it — reflexes become available with no LLM and no network.
parts.failure_mode: HONEST GAP: exportNail returns allReflexes() which is currently a demo stub returning [] (engine.ts:L155-L160) — bundles exported through this path are empty; esp32's buildNail is the working path

parts.name: platform sheets (cloud / workstation / esp32 defaults)
parts.essence: cloudSheet, workstationSheet (SQLite + sqlite-vec), esp32Sheet (in-memory, no LLM) return the same sheet with tier-appropriate stores and embedders — one code path, three compute tiers, matching the README's latency table.

parts.name: node:test suite (12 checks)
parts.essence: test/reflex.test.ts covers direct hit, trigger variation, confirm tier, compile tier with a mock compiler, veto refusals, confidence climb, sheet composition, and the three platform sheets incl. .nail loading — the repo's dog-food gate.
parts.gate: assert.equal(result.kind, 'hit') etc. — tier outcomes are the contract
parts.failure_mode: repo ships without node_modules/dist; tests need tsx from a sibling checkout (local-only workaround used for this audit)

parts.name: result kinds + latency telemetry
parts.essence: Every run returns a discriminated PinchResult — hit | confirm | compiled | vetoed | error — each carrying latencyMs measured from pinch start; the tier, the reason, and the cost are always observable downstream.
parts.gate: latencyMs recorded on EVERY outcome incl. errors and vetoes
parts.failure_mode: a vetoed or errored pinch still consumes the embedding call — latency telemetry shows it but does not refund it

parts.name: embedder degradation ladder
parts.essence: Embedder implementations form a degradation ladder: CloudflareAIEmbedder (network + key), QuiltAIEmbedder (quilt-ai), OfflineEmbedder, HashEmbedder — the same sheet runs with or without keys because the embedder is an interface, not a service.
parts.failure_mode: switching embedders changes the geometry: reflexes embedded by one model do not cosine-match queries embedded by another (store must be re-embedded)

cells.expr: {trigger, context, safety} arrives from the platform
watches execute paths; refuses escalation (network/filesystem/sandbox) before any run
new Function('pinch', action) raced vs executionTimeoutMs=5000

layer_logic.0: Substrate = two records and one geometry: the pinch envelope, the reflex record, and the embedding vector space every reflex lives in; all three are plain data so any tier (cloud to ESP32) can hold them.
layer_logic.1: Mechanisms = the reflex arc: embed -> query top-k -> route by score -> execute under timeout; plus the two learning loops — confidence climbs with hits, and the compile tier writes new reflexes so the fast tier grows.
layer_logic.2: Policy = the gates: 0.80/0.55 tier thresholds (routing), the veto's escalation refusals (admission to execution), the no-compiler fail-closed error, and the 5s execution budget — four pass/fail conditions the JEV sweep can walk.
layer_logic.3: Interface = PincherSheet's six-cell descriptor, runPinch, the three platform sheets, and the .nail bundle that ships the reflex database to offline engines.
layer_logic.4: Evidence = the discriminated result kind + latencyMs on every outcome, and the 12-check node:test suite; honest gaps recorded: allReflexes() stub returns [] so engine.exportNail exports empty bundles, and execute() is unsandboxed by its own admission.
